pairs: Truly, I know that it is so,
et quod non justificetur homo compositus Deo.
and that man cannot be justified compared with God.
If he chooses to contend with him,
non poterit ei respondere unum pro mille.
he is not able to respond to him once out of a thousand times.
et nescierunt hi quos subvertit in furore suo.
and those whom he overthrew in his fury did not know it.
Qui commovet terram de loco suo,
He shakes the earth out of its place
et stellas claudit quasi sub signaculo.
and he closes the stars as if under a seal.
and he walks upon the waves of the sea.
and the interior of the south.
whose wrath no one is able to resist,
et sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem.
and under whom they bend who carry the world,
et loquar verbis meis cum eo?
qui etiam si habuero quippiam justum,
And if I now have any justice,
And if he should listen to me when I call,
non credo quod audierit vocem meam.
I would not believe that he had heard my voice.
For he will crush me in a whirlwind
He does not permit my spirit to rest,
and he fills me with bitterness.
nemo audet pro me testimonium dicere.
no one would dare to give testimony for me.
If I wanted to justify myself,
my own mouth will condemn me;
if I would reveal my innocence,
And if I now became simple,
my soul would be ignorant even of this,
and my life would weary me.
There is one thing that I have said:
et innocentem et impium ipse consumit.
both the innocent and the impious he consumes.
let him kill all at once,
et non de pœnis innocentum rideat.
and not laugh at the punishment of the innocent.
Terra data est in manus impii;
Since the earth has been given into the hand of the impious,
he covers the face of its judges;
for if it is not him,
My days have been swifter than a messenger;
They have passed by like ships carrying fruits,
just like an eagle flying to food.
“By no means will I speak this way.”
and I am tortured with sorrow.
I have dreaded all my works,
knowing that you did not spare the offender.
if I am also just as impious,
why have I labored in vain?
Si lotus fuero quasi aquis nivis,
If I had been washed with snow-like waters,
et fulserint velut mundissimæ manus meæ,
and my hands were shining like the cleanest thing,
yet you would plunge me in filth,
and my own garments would abhor me.
Neque enim viro qui similis mei est, respondebo;
For even I would not answer a man who were like myself,
nec qui mecum in judicio ex æquo possit audiri.
nor one who could be heard with me equally in judgment.
Non est qui utrumque valeat arguere,
There is no one who could both prevail in argument
et ponere manum suam in ambobus.
and in placing his hand between the two.
Let him take his staff away from me,
et pavor ejus non me terreat.
and let not the fear of him terrify me.
and I will not fear him,
for in fearfulness I am not able to respond.
